_note: Every document the fire-ratings page cites. One record per document; product rows, decoder entries and jurisdictions refer to these ids. accessed = when we last opened it; issued, effective and statedExpiry are the document's own dates, never inferred (a validity period printed as 'five years from' a date is turned into that date and says so). sha256 is of the file we read, kept so a silent revision is noticed (npm run check:fire-sources -- --hash); the documents themselves are not stored in this repository.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Fire safety: Approved Document B (GOV.UK collection)
sources.establishes: GOV.UK's index of the current Approved Document B volumes and amendment booklets, with the change history.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 2: Buildings other than dwellings
sources.reference: 2019 edition incorporating the 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026 amendments, with the forthcoming 2029 changes; for use in England
sources.pages: Requirement B2 and Section 6, printed pp. 54–60 (Table 6.1, note 1 and paragraph 6.4 on p. 55); Appendix B, paragraphs B1 to B9, printed pp. 138–139
sources.establishes: England's current guidance on wall and ceiling linings in buildings other than dwellings: requirement B2, Section 6, Table 6.1 and its BS EN 15102 wallcovering note, the definitions of walls and ceilings, and Appendix B on reaction-to-fire classes, test evidence and substrates.
sources.limits: Guidance on one way of meeting requirement B2, not the law itself. Pages marked as 2029 amendments are not yet in force.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Approved Document B: Fire safety, Volume 2, 2019 edition incorporating the 2020 amendments and the 2022 amendments (superseded)
sources.pages: Table 6.1, printed p. 55; Appendix B, paragraph B10 and Table B1, printed pp. 137–138
sources.establishes: The previous edition, which still applies to work covered by the transitional arrangements. Its Appendix B and Table B1 set out the former national classes and warn that national and European classes do not automatically equate.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Amendments to Approved Document B, Volumes 1 and 2: taking effect on 2 March 2025
sources.pages: Introduction, p. 2; Volume 2 list of amendments, pp. 12–20
sources.establishes: The removal of national reaction-to-fire classes from England's guidance from 2 March 2025, and the transitional arrangements for work already notified.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Amendments to Approved Document B, Volumes 1 and 2: taking effect on 30 September 2026
sources.establishes: The 2026 changes (second staircases and evacuation lifts in blocks of flats), in force from 30 September 2026. They do not change lining classes.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Amendments to Approved Document B, Volumes 1 and 2: taking effect on 2 September 2029
sources.establishes: The removal of national fire-resistance classes from England's guidance on 2 September 2029, with transitional arrangements.
sources.limits: Not in force on the date we checked.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Approved Document B (fire safety): new updates to support enhanced fire safety
sources.establishes: The government's own explanation of the 2025, 2026 and 2029 changes, treating reaction to fire and fire resistance as separate subjects.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Circular 03/2024: Approved Document B (sprinklers and reaction to fire)
sources.establishes: The circular approving the 2025 amendments, including the removal of the national classification for reaction to fire.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Circular 05/2024: Approved Document B (fire resistance)
sources.establishes: The circular approving the 2029 amendments on the national classification for fire resistance.
sources.limits: Not in force on the date we checked.

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Approved Document B: fire safety, frequently asked questions
sources.reference: Question 18 (field of application of reaction-to-fire classes)
sources.establishes: Official answers on Approved Document B, including that the same material can achieve different classes in different forms, fixings and substrates, and that variations should be assessed by competent professionals.

sources.title: The Building Regulations 2010, Schedule 1, Part B, and regulation 7
sources.establishes: The legal requirement for internal linings (requirement B2 in Schedule 1 to the Building Regulations 2010) and regulation 7 on materials.

sources.title: Building Act 1984, sections 6 and 7
sources.establishes: The status of approved documents: approved under section 6, and under section 7 compliance or non-compliance may be relied on as tending to establish or negative liability.

sources.title: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, articles 3, 8, 9 and 50
sources.establishes: Fire safety in occupied premises in England and Wales: the responsible person's duties to take general fire precautions and to keep a fire risk assessment under review.

sources.issuer: Department for Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Fire safety risk assessment: sleeping accommodation
sources.reference: Guide published under article 50 of the Fire Safety Order
sources.establishes: Official fire risk assessment guidance for hotels and other sleeping accommodation in England and Wales, which discusses wall and ceiling linings and multiple layers of decorative finishes such as wallpaper, in the older national class terms.
sources.limits: Written before the European classes replaced the national ones in English guidance; it says the European equivalent is acceptable.

sources.issuer: Department for Communities and Local Government
sources.title: Fire safety risk assessment: offices and shops
sources.reference: Guide published under article 50 of the Fire Safety Order
sources.establishes: The equivalent official guidance for offices and shops, with the same treatment of wall and ceiling linings.
sources.limits: Uses the older national class terms.

sources.title: Approved Document B: fire safety (Wales)

sources.title: Amendments to Approved Document B, Volumes 1 and 2, coming into effect 20 December 2025 (Wales)
sources.establishes: The Welsh amendment slip in force from 20 December 2025. It concerns external walls and does not change the linings table.

sources.title: Building (Amendment) (Wales) Regulations 2025: circular WGC 004/2025
sources.establishes: The Welsh circular on the 2025 amendments. It says the proposed move of national classes into an appendix will follow the next revision of Approved Document B.

sources.title: Part B (fire safety): summary of responses and Government response
sources.establishes: The Welsh Government's consultation response: national classes are to move to an appendix rather than be deleted, and full removal would need further research and consultation.

sources.title: Construction Products Regulation in Great Britain
sources.establishes: How construction products are marked and declared in Great Britain: UKCA, and CE marking, which continues to be recognised, with a declaration of performance for products covered by a designated standard.

sources.title: Construction Products Regulation in Northern Ireland

sources.issuer: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

sources.limits: Proposals; not law.
